text:
**Short answer:** for most campers, a ~288Wh LiFePO4 unit is the sweet spot. For multi-day trips or a 12V fridge, step up to a Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 or 2000 v2.

## Weekend tent or car camping (about 250-300Wh)
This covers phones, lights, a camera, and a CPAP for a few nights. PowerStationGearLab recommends turning the CPAP humidifier off, since it can triple the draw. Prices are approximate.

- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (~$249, 288Wh, 8.3 lb, 300W): PowerStationGearLab's top pick for being light and simple. Jackery's own site has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, so it's mainly available through Amazon and other retailers. [Buy link on this page](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (~$269-299, 286Wh, 600W): double the Jackery's AC output, and expandable to 572Wh. Same page as above.
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (~$199, 288Wh, built-in LED lantern, 5-year warranty): make sure you buy the standard AC-outlet version, not the "C300 DC." Same page. Note that OutdoorGearLab's lab tests scored it low (50/100), so it's a value pick rather than a performance leader. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Bluetti EB3A** (~$179, 268Wh, 600W): the budget pick. Same PowerStationGearLab page. TechRadar's budget pick is the similar Bluetti Elite 30 V2 (288Wh, 600W). [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)

## Multi-day trips, a fridge, or van and overland use
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (~$799, 1,070Wh, 23.8 lb, 1,500W): TechRadar's "best for camping" and PowerStationGearLab's van pick. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** (under $900 on sale, list $1,499, 39 lb): OutdoorGearLab's top pick for off-grid camping. It has plenty of capacity and easy solar add-ons, but no battery expansion. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** (under ~$530 on sale): OutdoorGearLab's best value, though its fan is noisy. Same link.
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** (~$1,079-1,199): WIRED's camping pick. It's IP65-rated, drop-resistant, and about 40 lb. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)

## My pick
For a typical weekend of camping, I'd go with the **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** if you might run anything beyond small electronics, or the **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** if you want the lightest, simplest option. If you need to run a fridge or stay out for several days, get the **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2**.

## Caveats
- I couldn't open retailer pages, so I don't have direct product links. The review pages above have the current "check price" buttons, and prices change often (Black Friday is coming).
- Several of these sources earn affiliate commissions. OutdoorGearLab says it buys everything it tests, and it rated the small units lower than the smaller blogs did.
- Power stations are too large to take on planes, since they exceed the 100Wh lithium battery limit.

If you tell me what you'll power (CPAP, fridge, laptop) and how many nights, I can narrow it to one.
